summary: 43 units (44-86) reviewed against the Sanskrit, words and printed Devanagari. 5 errors, 36 minor. Errors: 47 kulīra stated as certain crab; 61 vāsa silently = vāsā and tagged standard; 77 unmarked conjectural uśīra, supplied 'when', wrong Hindi plural चित्रकों; 79 ācamana rendered only 'rinsing'; 82 Hindi gender (कहे गए विधि). Recurring: m./n. in gram for unstated nouns (vātike etc.), Hindi बस्ति is feminine, circular 'identifications' that repeat the Sanskrit name (vidārīkanda, pāṣāṇabheda, दन्तीमूल, gambhārī), modern names missing in some translations. Plant identifications spot-checked (hiṅgu, citraka, trivṛt, viḍaṅga, madanaphala, rājavṛkṣa, parūṣaka, khadira, arjuna, bhārgī, kuṭaja, śvadaṃṣṭrā, gavākṣī, mṛdvīkā, palāśa, dhātakī, sarala, dhava): none wrong. Regrouping: 56 should be split at 'vātaje' (first half continues 52-55, second half opens the ārtava section); 81 continues 80; 83-86 form one passage. Human decisions: 58 kalke/kalkaṃ, 77 hiṃguśīra and the duplicate hiṅgu/citraka, 74 hedge of kuṇapa-retas, 79 pairing, 55 pragāḍha sense, 84-86 'according to others'.
glossary_suggestions: Hindi बस्ति (enema) is feminine: तेल की बस्ति, दी जाने वाली बस्ति.
Hindi doṣa-type adjectives follow the Sanskrit suffix: -ika/-ya (vātika, paittika, ślaiṣmika) = वातिक, पैत्तिक, श्लैष्मिक; -ja = वातज, पित्तज, कफज.
ācamana = sipping (also rinsing the mouth); keep apart from prakṣālana (wash).
kulīra (p02 ch01 u47) = probably crab, hedged; kuṇapa-retas = probably semen of a corpse-like smell (hedged).
A modern identification must name something other than the Sanskrit synonym (not 'pāṣāṇabhedaka = pāṣāṇabheda', 'vidārī = vidārīkanda').
Dvandva in the plural instrumental (hiṅgūśīracitrakaiḥ) is one plural for the group; Hindi uses the singular for the last member (चित्रक से).
picu in yoni therapy = wad or swab of cotton (Hindi पिचु यानी रूई का फाहा); the measure sense (picu = karṣa) does not apply here.
pratīvāpa (long ī) as printed in 48, 52, 77; prativāpa in 44; w keeps the printed form, no flag.
